learningObjective: Explain what temperature and top-p sampling do at the logits/probability level.

canonicalClaims.claim: Temperature T divides logits by T before softmax; top-p (nucleus) sampling, after softmax, keeps the smallest descending-cumulative set whose sum first exceeds p, then renormalizes and samples from that set.
nonImplications: Does not imply top-p is equivalent to top-k.
Does not imply temperature affects relative rank exactly; extreme T can numerically flatten it.

misconceptions.claim: Temperature is applied to softmax outputs, not logits.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Standard definition applies T to logits before softmax; applying to outputs breaks the probability property.

misconceptions.claim: Top-p keeps a fixed fraction floor(p*V) of tokens by count.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Top-p uses cumulative probability, not count; the set size is adaptive.

misconceptions.claim: Top-p is equivalent to top-k under p = k / V.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Top-p adapts to distribution shape; top-k does not.

implementationFacts: vLLM, SGLang, TRT-LLM all implement temperature + top-p (+ optional top-k) as a fused sampling kernel.
Greedy decoding = T → 0 (or T=0 handled as argmax).
performanceScenarios: Sampling is a small fraction of decode time but must be latency-optimized because it is on the critical path per token.
